text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today after climbing strongly over the past week, pulling back from a $137 high just yesterday. The decline comes as oil prices retreated slightly—U.S. crude dropped to $91.48 per barrel—and reflects profit-taking after the stock had gained over 5% in five trading days. This pullback is modest and fits a normal trading pattern following a sharp run-up.

The broader backdrop remains mixed for oil majors. While refinery disruptions in Ukraine and Russia have pushed diesel to record highs, boosting margins for refiners in the short term, today's geopolitical news—including Argentina's threats against oil companies over the Falklands and continued sanctions on Iran—hasn't created the kind of supply shock that would sustain oil prices higher. The gains ConocoPhillips saw earlier this week may have reflected optimism about constrained refining capacity; today's pullback suggests that optimism has hit a ceiling as investors weigh competing forces.
